blocker_resolution_evidence.B1: capGuidanceItems is now an unconditional slice(0,3) with no priority-aware escape hatch; hiddenCount/requiredOverflowCount are computed from items.slice(3) only, so requiredOverflowCount can only ever count REQUIRED items genuinely absent from `visible` -- the factually false label is arithmetically impossible now. runGuidancePipeline no longer caps, so the complete ranked set exists as one shared object; deriveDashboardGuidance caps it and deriveAttentionGuidance renders it whole, both from the same deriveGuidanceItems call, so the two views cannot disagree. GuidanceWorkQueue renders ONLY cap.visible through GuidanceItemList and puts the overflow control outside the <ul> as a sibling <Link>, so it is structurally incapable of being a 4th item card; required overflow takes precedence over the generic 'See all' and links to /attention#required. /attention partitions the complete set into Required/Recommended/Optional, which is exhaustive over GuidancePriority and order-preserving (Array.filter is stable), so nothing is dropped and v2.1.1 ranking order survives. Proven by 9 shipped cap tests, my 4 independent boundary tests including the aggregate-at-cap case, and a real-browser E2E run.
blocker_resolution_evidence.B2: The 'D is DRAFT with an incomplete completeness_report' gate is gone: isNonMemberOfDeclarationInPeriod now reads ONLY declaration.member_shipment_ids, and neither declaration.status nor declaration.completeness_report is referenced anywhere in i19.ts. impact = declarationExistsForPeriod && !forcedToApproval ? FILING : APPROVAL, with priority hardcoded REQUIRED, actionability NAVIGATE and title 'Mark {ref} ready' unconditional -- so the item is never suppressed, merged, downgraded, or re-actioned. I verified all 24 cells of the status x completeness x membership matrix myself, including all four VOID cells that the shipped suite does not cover at all, and confirmed a member shipment's item is untouched in every cell.
blocker_resolution_evidence.B3: listDraftShipmentsWithLines chunks shipment ids at 100 per .in() and paginates every query via .range() with a stable, unique .order('id'); fetchAllPages throws on a query error instead of returning a partial or empty result. listDeclarations now throws too (the follow-up gap the pre-verification pass found). deriveGuidanceItems converts either throw into an explicit {status:'UNAVAILABLE'} that both deriveDashboardGuidance and deriveAttentionGuidance propagate, and both GuidanceWorkQueue and /attention render it as a role=alert error message that is textually distinct from 'Nothing needs your attention right now.' I confirmed live that the old shape really fails ('URI too long' at 1000 ids) and that the new one really works at 1200 shipments / 2640 lines past max_rows, with correct per-shipment attribution and no duplicates.

findings.description: One silent error-to-empty conversion still remains inside the guidance read path, contrary to the letter of the B3 remediation spec ('verify no silent error-to-empty conversion remains anywhere in the guidance read path'). listGuidanceDismissals is awaited in the same Promise.all as the two fetches that were fixed, but on a query error it returns an empty Set rather than throwing, so a dismissals-read failure can never reach deriveGuidanceItems's catch and can never surface as UNAVAILABLE. Not blocking, because the failure direction is the safe one: applyGuidanceDismissals only ever FILTERS OUT items whose id is in the set, so an empty set can only cause MORE items to be shown, never fewer -- it is structurally incapable of producing the false 'Nothing needs your attention right now.' that B3 exists to prevent. It is also pre-existing (untouched by this commit) and deliberately justified in the function's own doc comment as a fail-open choice matching getOrganizationSmeProfile. Worth closing for consistency so that 'a genuine fetch failure becomes UNAVAILABLE' holds for all three of deriveGuidanceItems's fetches rather than two of three.

findings.description: The new doc comment asserts 'This function's one real caller is deriveGuidanceItems', and the new test's description repeats it ('its one real caller is deriveGuidanceItems'). Both are factually false: app/(importer)/declarations/page.tsx:104 also calls it. Worse, the remediation's own diff DELETED the sentence that documented that caller ('The declarations list screen (master plan section 27 screen 22)'), so the change replaced accurate information with inaccurate information. The behavioral consequence is that the declarations list screen's failure mode silently changed too, from rendering a false empty list to throwing -- a change in the right direction (app/error.tsx exists, so it degrades to a proper error boundary rather than a crash, and a false 'no declarations' on a compliance screen is exactly the anti-pattern B3 targets), but one that was made on a premise the author had just written down as untrue and therefore did not analyse. Secondary: the thrown message is hardcoded 'guidance: declarations fetch failed (...)', which will be actively misleading in logs when the failure originated on the declarations screen rather than in guidance.
findings.evidence: src/application/declarations/list-declarations.ts:28-30 and :54-56; src/application/declarations/list-declarations.test.ts:90; second caller at app/(importer)/declarations/page.tsx:104. `git show e666878 -- src/application/declarations/list-declarations.ts` shows the screen-naming sentence being removed in the same hunk that adds the single-caller claim.

findings.description: The UNAVAILABLE conversion is implemented with a bare `catch {}` wrapping not just the fetches but also deriveI19Items and runGuidancePipeline -- pure domain code. A programming error in the domain layer (a TypeError in ranking, aggregation, or I19 derivation) is therefore indistinguishable from an infrastructure outage and is presented to the user as 'Couldn't load your guidance right now. Try refreshing the page.', which will never recover on refresh. Nothing is logged: the caught error is discarded entirely, so an operator gets no signal, no message, and no stack. The user-visible outcome is still the correct degraded state rather than a false all-clear, so this is not blocking and it matches an existing in-repo pattern (check-app-url.ts, check-product-schema.ts also swallow bare). But the whole point of B3 and its follow-up was to make failures visible, and this makes the CAUSE of a failure invisible. Narrowing the try to the `await Promise.all(...)` alone, and threading the error to the existing structured logger (src/infrastructure/observability/logger.ts) via a port, would close it without changing the contract.
findings.evidence: src/application/guidance/derive-guidance-items.ts:72-111 -- the try opens before the fetches and closes after runGuidancePipeline; the handler is `} catch { return { status: "UNAVAILABLE" }; }` with no binding and no logging. `grep -rn 'console\.' src/ --include=*.ts | grep -v test` shows the only logging site in src/ is src/infrastructure/observability/logger.ts, used solely by app/api/health/route.ts.

observations_not_findings: listDeclarations has no .range() pagination, so it would be silently truncated by PostgREST's max_rows=1000. Unreachable at any realistic declaration volume (declarations are one-per-reporting-period), the query shape is unchanged from before the remediation, and the spec's pagination requirement is scoped to .range()-paginated queries, of which this is not one. Noted rather than filed.

I19 is currently the only rule wired into deriveGuidanceItems, and it always emits priority REQUIRED with parent: null. Consequently the generic 'See all' overflow branch, the Dismiss button, and the entire aggregation path are all currently unreachable in the shipped product -- they are proven correct by unit tests (and, for the aggregate-at-cap case, by my own), not by any live path. Not a defect in this remediation; a scope fact worth carrying into S3.

fetchAllPages's correctness depends on PAGE_SIZE (1000) being <= PostgREST's max_rows (1000). If max_rows were ever lowered, the first short page would break the loop and silently truncate -- the exact failure class B3 targeted. The constant is documented as tracking config.toml and I confirmed both values live, so this is a latent coupling to note, not a present defect.
fetchAllPages's error message says 'guidance: draft shipment fetch failed' even when the failing query is the shipment_lines one. Cosmetic only.

summary: PASS. All three blocking findings from the prior review (7b0d54b) are genuinely resolved, and I confirmed each one empirically rather than by reading the diff. B1: the cap is now an unconditional slice(0,3) with no priority escape hatch, the pipeline no longer caps so one shared uncapped ranked set feeds both views, and the overflow control sits outside the card list as a sibling link -- verified by 9 shipped tests, 4 independent boundary tests of my own (including an aggregate item at the cap boundary, where I cross-checked requiredOverflowCount against an independently recomputed hidden-REQUIRED set), and a real-browser Playwright run against a production build that saw exactly 3 cards, the exact '1 more required item' label, the /attention#required href, and all 4 items on /attention. B2: i19.ts no longer references declaration.status or declaration.completeness_report at all; I verified all 24 cells of the status x completeness x membership matrix myself, including the four VOID cells the shipped suite never covers, plus multi-declaration, quarterly-period, and empty-snapshot edges. B3: I reproduced the old failure live ('URI too long' with 1000 ids) and then proved the new implementation at 1200 shipments and 2640 lines -- past PostgREST's max_rows, so both .range() loops actually ran, which the shipped 250-row test never exercises -- with correct per-shipment line attribution, preserved line ordering, and zero duplicate ids. Real errors throw, deriveGuidanceItems converts them to UNAVAILABLE, and both UIs render that distinctly from the empty state. No test was deleted and no assertion weakened: the cap assertions that disappeared are precisely the ones that encoded the B1 bug. Zero migrations and zero new tables in this commit, no protected regulatory or P14 surface touched, typecheck and the full 1964-test suite green. Three YELLOW findings, none blocking: one silent error-to-empty conversion still remains in the guidance read path (listGuidanceDismissals), though it fails open and so cannot produce the false all-clear B3 targets; list-declarations.ts's new doc comment and test both assert a single-caller claim that is false and that the same diff created by deleting the sentence naming the other caller, meaning that screen's failure-mode change went unanalysed; and deriveGuidanceItems's bare catch spans the pure domain pipeline as well as the fetches and logs nothing, so a domain bug would masquerade as an infrastructure outage with no operator signal. I also investigated a suspected latent bug -- the dismiss action revalidating only '/' while the remediation newly mounts the dismiss-bearing component on /attention -- and withdrew it after reading this repo's bundled Next 16.3.3 docs, which state that revalidatePath re-renders the current route. Scratch artifacts deleted, no rows left in local Postgres, no lingering processes, tree clean. This certification authorises nothing beyond the review itself: no push, no merge, no deploy, no S3 start.
